description: Figure 8(d) illustrates the performance of knowledge probing after editing with different methods on the Qwen2.5 language model, with accuracy measured as ACC (%) on the y-axis, which ranges from 60 to 80 percent and uses a linear scale, and the x-axis representing the Co-occurrence Number on a logarithmic scale spanning from 10^0 to 10^3. The plot contains five distinct lines, each corresponding to a different editing method: “Base” (black circles), “MEND” (brown triangles), “MEMIT” (purple diamonds), “IKE” (red triangles), and “ROME” (green squares). All lines show an upward trend as the co-occurrence number increases. The “Base” line starts at approximately 62% accuracy and ends near 69%. The “MEND” line begins at about 70% and rises to roughly 78%. The “MEMIT” line starts around 70% and ends near 78%. The “IKE” line begins at approximately 67% and increases to about 75%. The “ROME” line starts at approximately 75% and rises to nearly 80%. All lines remain relatively close together, with “ROME” consistently achieving the highest accuracy throughout the range of co-occurrence numbers.
